system: ESCG Tour Acquisition — Event-Driven Production Loop
objective: Generate qualified voluntary senior-living tour inquiries for Evanston/North Shore families, without pretending inquiries are confirmed tours.

authority.github_loop: May autonomously research, verify, analyze, prepare drafts, and make isolated, tested GitHub changes or review PRs in scope.
authority.external_messages: NOT OWNED BY THIS LOOP while existing session operator is active. Prepare drafts/proposals; no sending, posting, joining groups, or making commitments.
authority.site_publication: Do not merge to main, publish, or deploy. Keep tested code improvements in separate review PRs unless authority is explicitly transferred.
authority.excluded: No spending, invented claims, protected personal data, client records, privacy/form changes, employer endorsements, or safeguards bypass.

queue.task: Give families who open the free tour checklist PDF a disclosed route to the Westminster Place tour request; today the PDF is a dead end for the tour step.
queue.evidence: Operator metrics 16-17 Nov: 3 of 4 genuine Facebook-origin visitors opened the checklist PDF; 0 started the assessment or reached the tour form. The PDF (main, _dist/downloads/senior-living-tour-checklist.pdf, checked 2026-11-20) has exactly 3 link annotations: the homepage, Medicare Care Compare and IDPH assisted living. None goes to /?tour=form#plan-visit, and nothing printed mentions a tour request, while every guide and the homepage put a disclosed 'Ask about a tour here' line beside the same download. On a phone the PDF opens full-screen, so the most engaged visitors end on a page with no tour step. Sample is tiny; this is a structural gap, not a measured effect.

There is no HTML source in the repo (Chromium/Skia output), so a visible line means regenerating or editing the page content. Changing an owner-locked asset needs Joseph's yes.

Ask at evanstonseniorcareguide.com', linked to https://evanstonseniorcareguide.com/?tour=form#plan-visit, and relax the test to allow that one link. Then this loop opens a tested review PR (one page, < 200 KB, other links unchanged).

ready.text:
Back from a holiday visit and wondering whether a parent in Evanston or Skokie needs more help than they let on? Small things add up: an emptier fridge, a near-fall nobody mentioned, the stairs taking longer. It is hard to tell whether that points to assisted living, memory care or something else. I made a free six-question check (about two minutes) that suggests which kind of care fits and shows which answers led there, so you can judge the reasoning yourself. No sign-up: no name, email or phone, and your answers stay in your browser. It is a starting point for the family conversation, not a diagnosis.

Disclosure: I work at Westminster Place in Evanston. The guide is my own independent project, it includes an optional way to request a tour there, and I receive no referral fees.

opportunity_map.how_to_use: Every way of reaching Evanston and North Shore families that could be examined, with its status, so that idle is declared only when nothing here is open and no scout is due. A ready queue task that names a map_item is worked like any other task, one per run. Finish it by writing the verdict into the item (act, watch, drop, owner or waiting, with the reason and the date) and by updating channel_yield when a result was measured. A ready task that names a scout is a discovery run: answer the scout's question from its own kind of evidence, put every candidate through discovery.gate, add those that pass as open items with their source in the note, then update the scout (last_run_utc, next_due_utc, last_result, and interval_days by the cadence rule in discovery.cadence) and add one line to discovery.log. A discovery run that finds nothing is recorded the same way and is a complete result. In the same completion commit, if fewer than three tasks are ready, add work so the next run has some: first the highest-ranked open item (mark it queued), and when no item is open, the scout that is most overdue, if one is due. Rank by expected qualified reach times the chance the next step needs neither Joseph nor his browser, divided by effort; ties go in lane_order. For a new referral class prepare at most three proposals before a response is seen. A class with eight or more shipped actions and no response is closed to more of the same until the approach changes. Add a new item only for a class not already listed, with the evidence that suggested it; never a variation of a dropped class, and never something that only sounds plausible. When no item is open, no scout is due and nothing else is ready, stop without a commit (docs/ESC-TOUR-LOOP.md, rule 6). Never reopen an item without new evidence. Never queue a task whose only output is a document, a rewording or a cosmetic site change. Do not add an owner item for a small gain while Joseph has six or more open; keep it in the map item's note until one clears. Read the clock with date -u for every timestamp; never estimate a time. Authority is unchanged: research and preparation only; no sending, posting, form submission, merging or deploying.

discovery.gate: A candidate becomes a map item only if all five hold. 1 New: it is not on the map and is not a variation of a dropped class (the same audience by the same route). 2 Observed: a source URL or a row in the site's own data shows it exists; no source, no candidate; never add something because it sounds plausible. 3 A path to families: it names how Evanston or North Shore families at or near a senior-living decision would come to see the guide. 4 Legitimate and free: inside the platform's or organization's own rules, disclosed, $0, no unsolicited private messages, nothing in bulk. 5 A first step exists: for the loop (research and preparation), for the designated operator (inside its existing authority) or for Joseph (an owner item with the minutes it takes). A run that finds nothing passes nothing: record the run and its next due date and stop; that record is its result.
discovery.cadence: Effort follows yield. When a scout run adds or reopens at least one item, halve that scout's interval_days, not below 3. After two runs in a row that add and reopen nothing, double it, not above 60. Set next_due_utc to the run time plus interval_days.

package.after_merge: After the merge nothing else is needed. The merged commit is published automatically by the Claude task "ESCG publish after merge" (it looks every hour from 06:27 to 23:27 Chicago time): it checks that the commit is your merge, rebuilds the site, runs every test suite, publishes through Netlify as before, compares every changed page with what you merged, and sends you one notification: live, or not live and why.
package.about: The daily approval package (procedure step 7, DAILY PACKAGE). One pull request for Joseph to merge; the worker re-cuts it once a day. after_merge is changed only by a session that heard Joseph say how the site gets deployed.

addenda.rule: Since 27 Nov 2026 Make runs on its Core plan and its timer looks every 15 minutes. Session starts are no longer scarce and there is no daily budget of Make operations: wherever this procedure speaks of about three starts a day, of the day's Make operations being used, or of a timer that looks every 3 hours, that no longer applies. The helper's NEXT and WAKE are the rule: remaining eligible work and handoffs chain at once, also before the package window, and a session wakes when work is really due. Claude's usage is the limit now: keep the usage reserve, finish what you start, and still prefer the reviewer agent inside the session to a later session. Nothing else changes: ROLE AND LIMITS, the gate, the independent readers, the daily package and QUIET stay exactly as they are.

On Joseph's word of 27 Nov 2026 ("Make productive use of the refreshed capacity. Prioritize customer acquisition, SEO, business development, conversion improvements and discovering new growth opportunities."): open frontier questions are eligible work while the usage reserve has room (STATUS.frontier.starts_sessions). They wake a session and keep the chain going, and frontier.due stays true in a session until the list is done, the day's count is reached or time is up; so "it never starts a session by itself" and "at least one" no longer describe it. Answer them in the order of frontier.next, each to the full standard: read every source yourself; act, watch or drop. A question whose sources you cannot read from here gets the verdict watch naming what blocks it; never skip one and leave it open. Close with --stop-reason time at SESSION_MINUTES minus 15; the next session continues.

THE PROJECTS (Joseph, 27 Nov 2026: "Treat growth opportunities as projects worth developing, not checkboxes to complete."). STATUS.projects.due lists growth projects (planner/projects) whose next step is due: they come before frontier questions, sweeps and planning, right after the package and ready tasks. Work the first one deeply for most of the session: investigate with sources, write the strategy, build the asset, prepare the execution. Every step ends in an artifact (research file, branch, pull request, prepared handoff), recorded with project-step ID --run RUN --result TEXT --new-evidence NEXT [--resume-when UTC] [--lane STAGE] [--verdict waiting|won|failed|parked]. A failed project needs its evidence; then add a better one with project-add. A frontier act becomes a project, not one task.

planner.budget_note: Usage reserve, not a task cap: the worker, Joseph's own chats, the drafts routine, the Daily Report and the outreach operator all share one Claude Max allowance (a 5-hour window and a weekly limit that resets Monday 4:00 am Chicago). The worker stops starting sessions once its sessions add up to budget_hours_per_day in the last 24 hours (and budget_hours_per_week in 7 days, when set), then resumes on its own. Starting value 6 hours per 24 hours, to be calibrated against the usage readings. Joseph changes it with one word. planner.how_to_use: When status shows plan.due (fewer than low_water items in the pipeline and at least one lane neither waiting on Joseph nor cooling down), plan for at most two plannable lanes, best measured outcome first (python3 ops/loopctl.py outcomes --days 28: lane_visitors, plus 10 per inquiry and 5 per organization reply attributed to the lane), then by order. Gather the lane's evidence, put every candidate through the gate, add the survivors with source plan, then record the pass with plan-done. Finding nothing is a complete result and puts the lane on cooldown. A lane whose owner_wip reaches its limit takes no new tasks until Joseph or the operator clears items. Since 24 Nov 2026 (v4.3.2): when the pipeline is under low_water and no planning pass or sweep is left, status shows fallback.due and the session runs the independent backlog fallback, recording each avenue with explore (see planner/fallback/how). Since 27 Nov 2026 (v4.4): everything inside the open daily package counts as one item against a lane's limit (planner/package/counts_as_one); strategy holds the 12-month plan that ranks candidates; planner/frontier holds genuinely new opportunity questions, answered one per session before a session may stop for lack of work.
planner.gate: A candidate becomes a task only if all hold: (1) concrete evidence with its source and date, never a guess; (2) a stated, plausible effect on qualified visitors, inquiries, referrals or tours; (3) not already queued, done, dropped or waiting (dupes and key); (4) its output is a change, a business asset (guide, FAQ, checklist, comparison or research resource that families or Joseph will use), a prepared handoff or a verdict someone can act on, never only an internal note, a rewording or a cosmetic change; (5) the worker can finish it within ROLE AND LIMITS; (6) impact x confidence / effort (each 1-5) of at least min_score.

strategy.how_to_use: Read this object when you plan (step 6e), sweep, explore and review. It ranks work; it never widens ROLE AND LIMITS. A working target is a yardstick for the monthly review, not a forecast and not a result. Rank a candidate that advances an objective of the current quarter above an equal-scoring one. The programs name what compounds: each has a standing angle, lane or step where its next step is found, so the backlog refills from the plan and not only from events. The monthly review (task keyed strategy-review:YYYYMM, due when status shows strategy.review_due) rewrites the baseline, each objective's status, the programs' next steps and the frontier list from measured results, adds one entry to reviews/log, and puts a change of direction to Joseph as one lettered decision.

diagnosis: The visitors who can become tours are local, and almost all arrive from the operator's posts in local Facebook groups. Group rules cap that channel, so it needs prepared material on hand and other local sources beside it.

Search shows the guide for national Medicare questions at positions around 30: wide, too deep to be clicked, and mostly not local. The pages already inside the top 10 are Illinois program pages; local-intent queries barely show yet.
The path from a visit to a tour request cannot be measured at present, so conversion work is blind until the counts can be read again.
Nothing outside links to the guide, and asking by email has not worked. Listings have to be earned with things worth listing.
Verified work reaches families only through Joseph's merge of the daily package; the merge now publishes automatically.
strategy.time_split: Owner rule of 17 Nov 2026: about 80% customer acquisition, 15% conversion and measurement, 5% maintenance. An accuracy audit beyond what a reader reopened, or beyond one a session, is maintenance.
principles: Evanston first, then the North Shore; Illinois and federal rules support the local answer.
The guide stays independent: never rank or recommend communities, never present Westminster Place as a partner or as objectively better; the tour request stays optional.
No pop-ups, chat widgets, extra questions or walls of text, and no feature whose benefit cannot be measured.
One change per page element, then measure before changing it again.
Evidence before building: a query, a public question, a measured result or an official source; never a guess, a rewording or filler.
Publishing, merging, sending, posting, contacting, spending, privacy, consent and how Westminster Place appears wait for Joseph or his operator: one daily package, one merge.
This repository is public: no personal information, and nothing about money or business plans beyond the site itself.
